_meta.description: Curated counter-narrative library. These are the Tier-1 fallback when no local LLM is available, and the citation backbone when one is. Organized by narrative family, not detection trigger — detection is technique-based; this library is a resource the user chooses to deploy.
style_rules: Calm beats clever. The goal is the onlooker, not the poster.
Every claim carries a source a normal person can open.
Acknowledge the legitimate concern under the narrative when one exists.
Never fabricate precision. '60+ court cases' is checkable; invented percentages are not.

families.name: Stolen / rigged election claims
counters: Over 60 court cases challenging the 2020 election were dismissed or ruled against, including by judges appointed by the president making the claims. Courts require evidence; none held up.
Trump's own DHS called 2020 'the most secure election in American history,' and his Attorney General said the DOJ found no fraud that would change the outcome.
Fox News paid $787.5 million to settle a defamation suit over these claims — internal messages showed hosts privately calling them false while airing them.

families.name: Climate denial / delay
counters: Every major scientific body on Earth — every national academy of science, every major meteorological organization — confirms human-caused warming. The 'debate' exists in media, not in the data.
Exxon's own scientists projected today's warming with startling accuracy in the 1970s-80s; the company then funded public doubt about its own findings (Supran et al., Science, 2023).
The legitimate concern underneath: energy costs and jobs are real issues. That's an argument about transition policy, not about whether the physics is happening.

families.name: Vaccine conspiracy claims
counters: mRNA vaccines cannot alter DNA — mRNA never enters the cell nucleus where DNA lives, and it degrades within days. This is testable, taught-in-textbooks cell biology.
Billions of doses have been administered under the most intense safety surveillance in medical history; serious adverse events are rare, documented, and publicly tracked (VAERS/V-safe data is open).

The legitimate concern underneath: pharma companies do have bad incentives and real scandals. That's why safety data is collected by independent systems in dozens of countries that don't share those incentives.

families.name: Anti-trans panic narratives
counters: Every major US medical association — AMA, AAP, APA, Endocrine Society — supports access to gender-affirming care. The 'medical controversy' framing misrepresents where medical consensus actually sits.
The 'groomer' slur is a pre-verdict: it convicts a group of a crime with no case attached. Actual child-protection work names perpetrators, cases, and charges — check whether the post does.
Trans people are a fraction of a percent of the population and are far more likely to be victims of violence than perpetrators. Panic requires inverting that ratio; the data won't.

families.name: Invasion / replacement narratives
counters: Immigrants — including undocumented immigrants — commit crimes at lower rates than native-born citizens. This finding replicates across decades of studies, including in Texas's own state data.

'Great Replacement' is not analysis; it's a named white-nationalist conspiracy theory cited by multiple mass shooters. Language of 'invasion' and 'poisoning blood' has a documented history and a documented body count.
The legitimate concern underneath: border policy and labor competition are real debates. Real debates use numbers with denominators, not hordes and floods.

families.name: Soros / globalist puppet-master claims
counters: 'One rich Jew secretly controls world events' is the oldest antisemitic template in existence, with the name swapped each generation — Rothschild, then Soros. The structure is the tell.
Soros's political giving is public and FEC-searchable — and comparable or smaller than that of Musk, Adelson, Uihlein, Thiel, or the Koch network, whose donations rarely earn 'puppet-master' framing.
Ask the substitution question: would this post work identically with 'Koch' swapped in? If the outrage is name-specific, it's not about money in politics.

families.name: CRT / 'indoctrination' panic
counters: The strategist who built the CRT panic explained the play on the record: 'We have successfully frozen their brand... to annex the entire range of cultural constructions that are unpopular with Americans' (Christopher Rufo, 2021, public tweets).

Critical race theory is a graduate-level legal framework; the K-12 'CRT' bans in practice removed books about Ruby Bridges and Rosa Parks. The gap between the label and the banned material is the point.
Teaching documented history — redlining, the Tulsa massacre — is not shame training. If a curriculum claim scares you, ask to see the actual lesson plan; districts publish them.

families.name: Welfare queen / lazy poor tropes
counters: Most working-age SNAP recipients who can work, do work — the benefit subsidizes low wages more than idleness. The largest employers of benefit recipients are giant profitable retailers.
Corporate subsidies, tax expenditures, and bailouts dwarf anti-poverty spending. The 'handout' frame is applied selectively by income of recipient.
SNAP has among the highest fiscal multipliers of any federal spending (~$1.50+ per $1 in downturns, USDA/Moody's estimates) — food assistance is stimulus, not drain.

families.name: 'You can't trust ANY source' nihilism
counters: 'All media lies' doesn't free you from media — it just hands your feed to whoever says it loudest. Total distrust is not skepticism; it's a different kind of obedience.

Real verification is boring and available: court filings, 990 tax forms, FEC records, agency datasets. Outlets that cite them can be checked; outlets that say 'do your own research' while citing nothing can't.
Notice the asymmetry: the source telling you to trust no one always exempts itself.

technique_scripts._description: Generic counter-scripts keyed by detected technique — usable on any topic, including brand-new narratives.
technique_scripts.fear_appeal: This post wants you scared before it wants you informed. What specific, checkable event is it actually claiming? Strip the adjectives and see what's left.
technique_scripts.urgency: Nothing real is falsified by waiting twenty minutes to verify it. 'Share before it's too late' is a tell — truth doesn't expire.
technique_scripts.menace_construction: Invasion, flood, poison, vermin: when humans are described with contamination metaphors, you're being prepared to accept things done to them. That's the metaphor's job. It has a history.
technique_scripts.child_threat_leverage: Real child-safety reporting names cases, charges, and courts. If 'protect the children' arrives with zero case numbers, the children are a shield, not a subject.
technique_scripts.othering: Any post that sorts the country into 'real' people and enemies has stopped arguing and started recruiting.
technique_scripts.consensus_faking: 'Everyone knows' is what you say when you can't say 'here's the evidence.' Who, specifically? Counted by whom?
technique_scripts.ridicule_of_dissent: Calling doubters sheep isn't an argument — it's an inoculation against you checking.
technique_scripts.source_tribalism: 'Only we tell the truth' is the setup for never having to be right again. Claims that are true survive hostile checking; ask why this one needs protection from it.
technique_scripts.insider_knowledge: 'What they don't want you to know' feels good — that feeling is the product being sold. Secret knowledge that arrives via viral post isn't secret; it's marketing.
technique_scripts.identity_flattery: You're being complimented into agreement. A claim that needs to flatter you first doesn't trust its own evidence.
technique_scripts.savior_framing: Complex problems don't have one-man solutions; claims that they do are asking for your trust, not your judgment.
technique_scripts.vague_attribution: 'Experts say' — which experts? Where? A named source can be wrong in public; a phantom source can never be wrong at all. That's why it's phantom.
technique_scripts.cherry_stats: A number without a denominator is a vibe in a suit. Up 300% — from what baseline? Out of how many? Compared to when?
technique_scripts.certainty_inflation: 'Proven beyond all doubt' is how contested claims dress up. Actual findings ship with error bars, methods, and rivals who checked.
technique_scripts.loaded_question: 'Just asking questions' smuggles the claim in the question. Notice you're expected to remember the insinuation, not the answer.
technique_scripts.hedge_laundering: 'Some say' launders an assertion through people who are never named. The author gets the claim's impact without the claim's accountability.
technique_scripts.stakes_inflation: The bigger the claimed stakes, the more evidence the claim owes you. 'End of America' + zero citations is a debt the post has no intention of paying.
